text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — proposing we push a compact cost-hint into edge proxies to avoid the expensive per-trace join in the ingest pipeline. idea: services compute a small billing hint (not authoritative) and add header `X-Redwood-Cost-Hint`. server-side resolver can verify/override. looking for concerns: security, accuracy, fallback behavior.

maria: worried about trusting service-side computation. what's the attack/threat model? a misconfigured service could poison cost attribution and leak billing to wrong tenant. also curious about retention / PSI if we add this header to logs.

jamal: perf numbers? how many extra bytes per request and CPU overhead on edge? if we add HMAC validation that increases CPU. but current join on the backend is >2x cost during spikes. pushing small hints might reduce downstream fanout.

alex: rough numbers from prototype: hint is 16 bytes (base64 22 chars) + header overhead ~40B. HMAC check adds ~200ns per request on optimized C path. Backend join savings: ~1.2ms median and spikes 5-10ms under load.

tina: suggested hybrid pattern: edge emits `X-Redwood-Cost-Hint: <hint>` plus `X-Redwood-Cost-Provenance: tentative`. In ingest we treat tentative hints as hints only: accept them if lookup matches or emit a correction event when we override. that keeps correctness and gives immediate routing improvements.

maria: +1 on provenance flag. also propose signed hints: services sign with an ephemeral key from KMS (rotate frequently) so ingest can validate signature cheaply, otherwise fall back to full lookup. prevents random spoofing.

jamal: question about key distribution to ephemeral service identities. if many small services use KMS per-request signing, cost could explode. maybe edge should sign using a local key cached by the proxy rather than each service calling KMS.

alex: agree — plan: service supplies mapping input (tenant id candidate or attributes) to proxy, proxy computes signed hint and attaches header. proxy has short-lived key material (rotated by control plane). that keeps service work minimal.

maria: what about privacy and PII? if hint is derived from user identifiers we must hash/pepper before encoding. need doc on what attributes are allowed.

alex: yes — we will restrict inputs to tenant-level attributes only (tenant id, org id, route id) and forbid user-level ids. addition: canonicalize and salt before hashing.

jamal: fallback policy details: ingest pipeline should treat hint precedence as: 1) validated signed hint -> accept, 2) unsigned but tentative hint -> attempt cheap lookup, if mismatch -> emit correction, 3) no hint or invalid -> full lookup. Also emit metric `ingest.cost_hint.override_count`.

alex: exactly. add SLOs: overrides <0.5% globally and <1% per-tenant; instrumentation available in console.

maria: deployment plan? canary in us-west1 edge proxies -> enable header attach, then enable validation in ingest as passive (emit metrics but not change billing) for 2 weeks, then switch to active override when stable.

alex: proposed rollout steps added: 1) spec PR for header + provenance + signing, 2) proxy key-rotation CR, 3) ingest passive validation + metrics, 4) canary attach + passive, 5) active override opt-in per-customer, 6) global active.

jamal: one more: need test harness to simulate mismatch scenarios and ensure we never double-bill or lose billing attribution on override. suggest creating e2e test that injects invalid hints and checks correction event path.

alex: good call, will add test plan.

sre-bot: deploy note: canary config bundle created: `edge-cost-hint-canary:v1` — ensure feature flag `edge_cost_hint` toggled off by default.

alex: thanks everyone — I'll file the follow-up RFC with the spec + rollout plan and tag infra/edge for key rotation work. if no objections I'll open the PR tomorrow.
